headline: High: dexter’s broad network/API use can leak or act on ComfyUI outputs, while shared-file and prompt-injection paths are limited by ComfyUI’s offline, no-read/write profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP surface and works fully offline, so direct injection into dexter is not documented. However, dexter uses autonomous execution with broad network/API access, so if operators bridge ComfyUI outputs into dexter via files or copy-paste, prompt-like content could influence downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is possible but not default.
conditions: IF operators manually copy ComfyUI-generated text into dexter prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file or queue is introduced between the agents, dexter may ingest attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste between outputs and prompts.
Add a human review step before dexter consumes any ComfyUI-generated text.
Use a one-way export format with strict schema validation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts, while dexter touches financial and market data and sends requests to multiple external APIs. There is no shared filesystem documented, but dexter’s broad egress means any ComfyUI-derived content routed into it could leave the local environment. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into dexter inputs, those contents may be transmitted to third-party APIs.
IF the operator stores both agents’ artifacts in the same directory, accidental disclosure becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI artifacts out of dexter’s scratchpad.
Redact sensitive fields before any dexter API call.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Review outbound API payloads for accidental inclusion of local files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and dexter’s documented mutable surface is limited to its scratchpad plus API calls. That means there is no strong write-write conflict on the same resource in the profiles. A conflict could appear only if an operator maps both agents onto the same external workspace, so the blast radius is small and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator shares mutable state without locking, race conditions may occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid sharing git repositories between the agents.
Run only one writer per workspace.
Check for lock files before launching dexter.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution and broad API access make it likely to act on upstream content, while ComfyUI can generate workflows and artifacts that may be treated as inputs. There is no explicit verification boundary in either profile, so if ComfyUI output is forwarded to dexter, errors can cascade into external API calls or incorrect research actions. The pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF dexter consumes ComfyUI output without a validation step, incorrect content can propagate downstream.
IF dexter is configured to execute actions from imported artifacts, the cascade can affect external services.
mitigations: Insert a manual verification step between agents.
Require schema checks on any transferred artifact.
Limit dexter to read-only analysis for ComfyUI outputs.
Log and review all downstream API actions.
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly handles financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, while ComfyUI is an offline image-generation system with local model files. If regulated financial data is routed through ComfyUI artifacts or mixed into its workspace, retention and residency controls can diverge from dexter’s API-driven processing. The profiles do not document a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is stored in ComfyUI artifacts, retention controls may differ from dexter’s API logs.
IF the operator exports dexter data into ComfyUI’s local files, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ComfyUI outputs.
Review API retention settings for dexter.
Separate datasets by classification.
Document which agent processes which data class.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention policy enforcement.
